reckon/crew/runs.py:2801 `watch_log_path` the single resolver both routes call

findings.text: the seat names `log_path` on every arming route while only the ensure route writes it: `dispatch._ensure_watch_producer` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3802, reached from admission) arms the same producer `_arm_watcher_as_process` does — the runs.py:2492 docstring says so — through `_start_watch_producer` (dispatch.py:824-831) with stdout and stderr on DEVNULL and never sets `WATCH_LOG_ENV` (dispatch.py contains no mention of it), and the fleet-delegated spawn cannot carry it either because its spec payload is `{"project","argv"}` (dispatch.py:816); so a producer armed that way leaves a seat pointing at a file nothing wrote, the `unit` key beside it showing the same file records only what is true of the route (runs.py:1632-1635).

the descriptors are pointed at the log once at adoption and rotation replaces the path without re-pointing them (runs.py:2843-2852), so after the first rotation a write through fd 1 or 2 lands in the `.1` generation and after the second the inode is unlinked and the write is lost — measured in gate/rotation-probe-two.log (`DESC1 in .1 True` then `DESC1 in .1 after rot2 False` and `DESC2 in .1 False and DESC2 in main False`) against the adoption docstring's claim that the descriptors exist so an interpreter traceback or a library's unbuffered write still lands in the log (runs.py:2896-2898); rotation is triggered only by the Python stream's own writes so a descriptor-only writer is never bounded at all.

the header names the base revision as head (`# head c0f6c8eabe2a517d526e04770fc0ce0a360144ea tree=<the reviewed worktree>`) because it ran on the uncommitted worktree three minutes before the change was committed as 75007b74, so its 3 failed 119 passed result cannot be tied from the log alone to a revision and a reader sees the head arm apparently running at base.

item_verdicts.diff: read the five-file diff against base — runs.py gains `WATCH_LOG_ENV`, `WATCH_LOG_MAX_BYTES`, `watch_log_path`, `_WatchLogStream` and `_adopt_watch_log` and names the log in the claim and in the rendered unit; the test file holds four tests including a real child that raises; the landing record, evidence anchor and figure reuse the plan's existing shapes.
item_verdicts.done_when: the three named tests are red at base and green at head — the base arm's 3 failures are `AttributeError: module 'reckon.crew.runs' has no attribute 'watch_log_path'` (gate/base-newtests-074040.log) so none passes vacuously, and my re-run of the same file at the committed head is 4 passed (gate/head-rerun.log, whose header names tree, revision 7ddc2a4b and command) — and the same three failures in tests/test_follow_counts_its_session.py reproduce at base (3 failed 1 passed, gate/base-followcounts-073905.log) against the head watchset's 3 failed 119 passed, a delta of zero, though that arm cannot be tied to the head revision from its own log (finding 3).
item_verdicts.goal: the named route works end to end — `crew watch --ensure` with no service manager names the log in the child's environment (reckon/crew/runs.py:2506) and the fork carries it, so the watcher adopts the file as it takes its seat (runs.py:1614), every line is timestamped and the seat names the path (runs.py:1629) — but the seat names `log_path` on every arming route while two of them never write it (finding 1), and the size bound and the descriptor capture stop holding at the first rotation (finding 2).
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records both commits, the gate command naming the run's own interpreter absolute path (which I ran as written), the head result 4 passed, the base arm, the declared control's log with its one-line note, and it leaves the driving followup open for the coordinator as the dispatch contract requires.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the five declared write paths; every path in c0f6c8ea..7ddc2a4b lies inside them, the plan and archive edits are pure insertions, the figure parses as XML under ElementTree and no changed line carries a plan label, ticket id or attribution.

justifications.durability: the declared mutation reddens two tests as its own log shows, but no test pins the size bound or the rotation — emptying `_rotate_if_needed` leaves all four green — and the descriptor loss in finding 2 is untested.
justifications.evidence: the base arm is non-vacuous and I reproduced the file gate at the committed head with the header naming tree revision and command, but the wider 119-passed arm ran on the uncommitted worktree three minutes before its commit and its header names the base revision (finding 3), so only the file gate is tied to a revision the log shows.
justifications.fit: the figure parses, the landing record and evidence anchor follow the plan's existing shapes, and the new comment at runs.py:1611 states the invariant the dispatch route breaks, which is the one place a later reader would not look.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the ensure route writes a timestamped log the seat names and both routes resolve one path (reckon/crew/runs.py:2801), but a producer armed by an admission (dispatch.py:3802) or by the fleet-delegated spawn keeps DEVNULL output while its seat still names a path (finding 1), so the record's promise holds on one of three arming routes.
justifications.scope_discipline: exactly the five declared paths changed, the shared plan and archive files receive pure insertions, and naming checks over the changed lines find no plan label, ticket id or attribution.
